Americans have never been this pessimistic about their finances:

A record 41% of US consumers expect their financial situation to be worse over the next 12 months.

This figure has more than tripled since Q2 2024.

By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, this metric peaked at 23%.

This proportion is also significantly higher than in the 1970s and the 1980s, when CPI inflation was above 10%.

Furthermore, 31% of US consumers believe their personal financial situation will be worse in 5 years, double the proportion seen in the 1980s.

Americans feel as though we are in a recession.

On days like today, it's important to zoom out.

No, the AI Revolution is not "over," and the market is not "going to zero."

In fact, the Nasdaq 100 is up +11% YTD and nearly +70% since its April 2025 low.

Meanwhile, the S&P 500 is currently set to post a blended earnings +30.2% growth rate for Q3 2026.

This puts us on track for the third-straight quarter of earnings growth above 25%.

And, even after the biggest hack in crypto history, Bitcoin is down less than -5% this week.

Disruptive technologies like AI will inevitably bring heightened volatility, polarized positioning, and extreme swings in market sentiment.

However, do not let short-term volatility overshadow the broader picture.

We are in the midst of the biggest technological revolution in history.

Technical corrections are healthy, necessary, and an inevitable part of every bull market.

Do not lose sight of the bigger picture.

With bonds providing a port in the storm for now, it’s a reminder that bonds have become a viable asset class again, regardless of their sometimes-lacking anti-correlation credentials. They may not continue to be that port in the storm for long, but at least we are getting paid to take the risk (via high real yields).

This could be the worst last day of the month in October since 2009 when it fell 2.81%. That was also a Friday.

Gained six days in a row after that, fell 0.01%, and then up another day.

The timing of today's market crash is noteworthy.

As selling pressure spreads, the Nasdaq 100 is now down nearly -5% on the day.

Meanwhile, the market-implied odds of a Democrat "sweep" in the Midterms next week has surged from 65% to 72% today, a record high.

That's +7 percentage points in 2 days amid this market downturn.

We have yet to receive a comment from the Trump Administration regarding the current situation in the market.

However, what is clear is that the timing of today's market crash will be consequential.

And, even as technology stocks drop sharply, US Treasury Yields are barely seeing any relief.

This leaves us with high rates, a falling stock market, $100+ oil prices, and rising CPI, PPI, and PCE inflation.

Next week is going to be interesting, to say the least.

History shows that the higher nominal yields go, the more correlated bond and equity returns become. Makes sense since the risk asset must compete against the risk-free asset. In the chart below I show the 10-year yield on the horizontal axis and the 2-year (104-week) correlation of equity and bond returns on the vertical. The size of the dots shows the 13-week correlation to highlight periods when secular regimes of positive correlations are interrupted by short bouts of negative correlations. At 5% we are currently in the “low positive” correlation regime, not unlike the late 1990’s. That suggests to me that the current growth scare (which has produced a negative 13-week correlation) will ultimately give way to the prevailing trend of positive correlation.
Some of these stocks are going to get buyout bids at these levels.

Reddit's earnings call has exposed the new reality for thousands of companies.

"AI mode does not drive traffic. Not for us and not to anybody as far as I know. It used to be a traffic driver. Now it's not." - Reddit CEO.

The reality is that AI is fundamentally changing the way that humans access the internet.

Just 24 hours prior to this statement, Google's stock erased -$480 billion on the same issue: AI is disrupting the traditional search model.

For decades, the internet operated on a simple model. Search engines directed users to websites, and those websites monetized the traffic.

AI is destroying this business model, and it's happening at an accelerating pace.

The traditional model of internet traffic is rapidly becoming outdated.

The internet has entered a new era.

It’s not that every person necessarily wants to run their own local systems; it’s that some nontrivial percentage want/need to do that.

Businesses and individuals protective of their data privacy, or wanting to analyze/perform things that centralized providers might block from being analyzed/performed.

Obviously both datacenters and local setups are useful, depending on the context.
Same thing happens to the algo and HFT systems of old -- the AI combats will end up picking each others' pockets
